groups.label: Synthetic diagnostic tasks and model mechanisms

works.label: Peano
works.title: Giuseppe Peano, Arithmetices principia, 1889
works.idea: Peano gave arithmetic a small explicit stock of symbols and principles. Successor is a basic operation from which more elaborate arithmetic can be defined.
works.opulse: User selected atoms play the role of an explicit starting vocabulary.
works.borrow: Compare concept growth under different minimal atom sets.
works.adds: Executable generated definitions and answer checks for arithmetic tasks.

works.label: Schönfinkel
works.title: Moses Schönfinkel, On the Building Blocks of Mathematical Logic, 1924
works.idea: A small stock of combinators can express functional constructions without bound variables. This makes the choice of primitives and composition rules central.
works.opulse: Atoms and substitutions define which concepts can be built.
works.borrow: Test equivalent rules written with different surface syntax and count their description lengths.
works.adds: A bounded executable domain with exact values for model tasks.
works.note: Opulse uses variables and is outside a variable free calculus.

works.label: Gödel
works.title: Kurt Gödel, On Formally Undecidable Propositions, 1931
works.idea: Gödel encoded formal expressions and proofs as numbers so that relations among them could be treated arithmetically. His result concerns limits of formal proof.
works.opulse: Written derivation steps can be represented and checked mechanically.
works.borrow: Keep a compact certificate and the first invalid step for each proposed derivation.
works.adds: Fresh executable concept families and automatic step labels.
works.note: Gödel’s incompleteness result is outside this correspondence.

works.label: Church & Turing
works.title: Alonzo Church, An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory, 1936; A. M. Turing, On Computable Numbers, 1936 manuscript, 1937 volume
works.idea: Lambda terms and machines give different precise accounts of effective computation. Universal computation also brings undecidable questions.
works.opulse: Its definitions are programs interpreted under explicit semantics.
works.borrow: State the language boundary and the domain on which equivalence or termination can be established.
works.adds: A deliberately restricted generator that yields checkable finite tasks.
works.note: Opulse makes no claim of universal expressiveness.

works.label: Kleene
works.title: Stephen C. Kleene, General Recursive Functions of Natural Numbers, 1936
works.idea: Composition and primitive recursion build total functions from initial functions. Unbounded minimization extends the construction to partial recursive functions, since a search may never find a witness.
works.opulse: Substitution, branch choice, and bounded self calls build its generated operators; the bound keeps evaluation finite.
works.borrow: Report which functions its actual grammar permits and measure cost as the recursion bound changes.
works.adds: Controlled rule generation, traces, and benchmark labels.
works.note: Opulse fixed shapes cover a subset of primitive recursion. Conditional choice is a program form outside Kleene’s primitive recursive closure operators.

works.label: Child machine
works.title: Alan Turing, Computing Machinery and Intelligence, 1950
works.idea: Turing proposed educating a learning child machine. He also discussed variation and selection in training.
works.opulse: Concepts can arrive in dependency order.
works.borrow: Compare layer ordered, random, and reversed curricula with equal training budgets.
works.adds: Exact prerequisites and final answers.

works.label: Grzegorczyk
works.title: Andrzej Grzegorczyk, Some Classes of Recursive Functions, 1953
works.idea: Subrecursive classes distinguish families by the growth and recursion they permit. One label such as “recursive” hides substantial complexity differences.
works.opulse: Layer and recursion settings vary structural cost.
works.borrow: Record output growth, rewrite count, and execution cost separately from prompt length.
works.adds: Fresh operators and observable learner errors for each setting.
works.note: Opulse layers are distinct from Grzegorczyk levels.

works.label: Description length
works.title: Ray Solomonoff, A Formal Theory of Inductive Inference, 1964; A. N. Kolmogorov, Three Approaches to Information, 1965; Jorma Rissanen, Modeling by Shortest Data Description, 1978
works.idea: Short generating descriptions supply a principled preference among hypotheses that fit observations. Practical code length depends on the chosen language.
works.opulse: Definition size and library compression can measure one concrete description length.
works.borrow: Compare shortest consistent rules with model proposals and test the effect of atom choice.
works.adds: A finite search grammar with known ground truth.
works.note: Opulse code length depends on its grammar and is not universal Kolmogorov complexity.

works.label: Good
works.title: I. J. Good, Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine, 1965
works.idea: Good argued that a machine capable of designing better machines could start a succession of improvements. It is a conceptual argument, not an implemented algorithm.
works.opulse: Concept self play can test whether repeated operator invention helps on fixed tasks.
works.borrow: Measure gains on fixed held out libraries after each round.
works.adds: A finite test bed for one narrow feedback loop.
works.note: Operator invention alone does not establish improvement in machine design.

works.label: Gold
works.title: E. Mark Gold, Language Identification in the Limit, 1967
works.idea: A learner can revise hypotheses as evidence arrives and eventually stabilize on a correct grammar under specified conditions. The evidence protocol determines which classes are identifiable.
works.opulse: A hidden rule learner can revise candidate definitions after each observation.
works.borrow: Record hypothesis changes and stabilization, while distinguishing positive examples from chosen queries.
works.adds: Finite, generated target programs with exact test outputs.
works.note: Gold studied language identification. Opulse uses numerical operators.

works.label: Bongard & ARC
works.title: Mikhail Bongard, Pattern Recognition, English edition 1970; François Chollet, On the Measure of Intelligence, 2019
works.idea: Bongard problems ask a solver to state the rule separating two sets of visual examples. ARC emphasizes acquiring a skill on unfamiliar tasks with limited prior examples and experience.
works.opulse: A hidden operator can be inferred from a small input and output sample.
works.borrow: Plot equivalent rule recovery against example count, query budget, and prior exposure.
works.adds: Generated program rules and exact tests on fresh inputs.
works.note: The visual tasks also require perception.

works.label: Language of thought
works.title: Jerry Fodor, The Language of Thought, 1975; Steven Piantadosi, Joshua Tenenbaum, and Noah Goodman, Bootstrapping in a Language of Thought, 2012
works.idea: Structured representations can combine parts into new meanings. The later model studies how a system of number concepts can be learned from simpler conceptual resources.
works.opulse: Layered operators are an explicit language of compositional concepts.
works.borrow: Change the atom set and reveal layers in stages to test which intermediates are learned.
works.adds: Many fresh, exactly evaluable concept systems.
works.note: Observed behavior alone cannot establish an internal language of thought.

works.label: AM
works.title: Douglas Lenat, AM, 1976
works.idea: AM used an agenda and heuristic rules to construct and investigate mathematical concepts. A useful discovery had to support further exploration, not merely be syntactically novel.
works.opulse: Generated operator layers and proposed hidden intermediate concept tasks.
works.borrow: Rank inventions by reuse and reduction of held out solution length.
works.adds: Known generating definitions, exact values, and dependency records.

works.label: BACON
works.title: Patrick Langley, BACON, 1977; Langley, Simon, Bradshaw, and Żytkow, Scientific Discovery, 1987
works.idea: BACON searched observations for regularities and built derived quantities that made laws expressible. The later account treats discovery as choices of representation, hypothesis, and test.
works.opulse: Querying a hidden operator and proposing intermediate computations.
works.borrow: Score query choice, intermediate idea, and final rule separately.
works.adds: A known executable target and exact query answers.
works.note: Empirical science has noise and interpretation beyond the standard Opulse task.

works.label: Truth maintenance
works.title: Jon Doyle, A Truth Maintenance System, 1979; Stuart Feldman, Make, 1979
works.idea: Truth maintenance records justifications so revised assumptions can update dependent beliefs. Make rebuilds artifacts affected by changed prerequisites.
works.opulse: Its operator dependency graph tells which derived values require recomputation.
works.borrow: Record provenance for each answer and compare predicted affected nodes with actual changed values.
works.adds: Exact semantics for whether a dependency edit changes a given numerical answer.
works.note: The link concerns dependency tracking. Belief revision and software builds have different semantics.

works.label: ACT R
works.title: John Anderson, Acquisition of Cognitive Skill, 1982; Rules of the Mind, 1993
works.idea: Skill acquisition can turn interpreted knowledge into more direct procedures with practice. ACT R distinguishes stored knowledge from productions that use it.
works.opulse: A model may move from reading definitions to handling frequent ◆₁ like a familiar unit.
works.borrow: Compare accuracy, latency, and reasoning length for frequently practised and newly defined operators.
works.adds: Exact intermediate values and controlled practice frequency.
works.note: Model speed is an indirect measure of ACT R productions.

works.label: EURISKO
works.title: Douglas Lenat, Eurisko, 1983
works.idea: EURISKO extended discovery to heuristics that guide search, as well as domain concepts. The representation and search guidance shaped what it found.
works.opulse: An agent can choose candidate operators and change one search heuristic in a discovery experiment.
works.borrow: Let it change one heuristic at a time and measure validity, diversity, reuse, and solver difficulty.
works.adds: An interpreter that checks candidate operators in a constrained language.
works.note: The link concerns experiment design. Heuristic invention requires an agent around the interpreter.

works.label: PAC
works.title: Leslie Valiant, A Theory of the Learnable, 1984
works.idea: The PAC framework asks whether a class can be learned to specified error and confidence with bounded data and computation. The example distribution is part of the claim.
works.opulse: Operator rules can be sampled under controlled input and frequency distributions.
works.borrow: Report error by distribution and sample budget, including shifted input ranges.
works.adds: The target definition and exact evaluator are known.
works.note: Benchmark accuracy alone does not give a PAC guarantee.

works.label: Soar
works.title: John Laird, Paul Rosenbloom, and Allen Newell, Chunking in Soar, 1986; Allen Newell, Unified Theories of Cognition, 1990
works.idea: Soar learns reusable rules from successful problem solving. Newell also argued that a cognitive account should explain several kinds of behavior within one architecture.
works.opulse: A learned intermediate operator might shorten later computations across evaluation, inversion, and equivalence tasks.
works.borrow: Test the same learner on several task forms before and after repeated use of an operator.
works.adds: A common generated library with exact labels across those forms.
works.note: Opulse is a task generator rather than a cognitive architecture.

works.label: Angluin
works.title: Dana Angluin, Learning Regular Sets from Queries and Counterexamples, 1987
works.idea: A learner asks membership questions, proposes a hypothesis, and receives a counterexample when it is wrong. The method uses the information in counterexamples efficiently.
works.opulse: Black box operator evaluation supplies membership style answers; a solver can test a proposed definition.
works.borrow: Compare active queries, random queries, and counterexample guided revision by query count.
works.adds: A generated grammar of numeric operators with exact evaluation of candidate definitions.
works.note: The link concerns the query protocol. Angluin’s theorem does not transfer to this grammar.

works.label: Meta learning
works.title: Jürgen Schmidhuber, Evolutionary Principles in Self Referential Learning, 1987
works.idea: This work considers learning mechanisms that can themselves be modified.
works.opulse: A proposer could alter the strategy that chooses new operators, in addition to producing operators.
works.borrow: Freeze a held out evaluation set and compare successive proposer versions.
works.adds: Exact semantic checks and measured task utility for candidate operators.
works.note: Changing a generation policy is narrower than general meta learning.

works.label: Systematicity
works.title: Jerry Fodor and Zenon Pylyshyn, Connectionism and Cognitive Architecture, 1988
works.idea: The authors argued that related recombinations should be linked in a system with structured representations. The challenge is about patterns of competence, not one isolated correct answer.
works.opulse: Known operators can be placed in unseen expression positions and compositions.
works.borrow: Report paired success on a learned pattern and a matched recombination.
works.adds: Fresh symbols and exact compositional relations.
works.note: The link gives a behavioral probe. It does not prove a form of representation.

works.label: Predicate invention
works.title: Stephen Muggleton, Inductive Logic Programming, 1991; Muggleton, Lin, and Tamaddoni Nezhad, Predicate Invention Revisited, 2015
works.idea: Logic program induction uses examples and background predicates to learn rules. Invented predicates can shorten and generalize an explanation.
works.opulse: Chosen atoms are background operations and hidden intermediate operators are reusable invented functions.
works.borrow: Compare learning with and without permission to invent a helper operator.
works.adds: Exact outputs and a recorded target dependency graph.
works.note: The systems use different rule languages.

works.label: Curriculum
works.title: Jeffrey Elman, The Importance of Starting Small, 1993; Yoshua Bengio and colleagues, Curriculum Learning, 2009
works.idea: Both study whether a learning order that begins with simpler material helps later acquisition. The benefit depends on the learner and training conditions.
works.opulse: Layer, depth, recursion, and definition count can be varied separately.
works.borrow: Compare schedules at equal token budgets and common final evaluation.
works.adds: Known prerequisite graphs and several structural difficulty measures.
works.note: The link concerns controlled curriculum tests.

works.label: Copycat
works.title: Douglas Hofstadter and the Fluid Analogies Research Group, Fluid Concepts and Creative Analogies, 1995
works.idea: Copycat explores analogies among small letter string problems while allowing descriptions to shift with context. Structural correspondences matter more than literal symbol matches.
works.opulse: Renamed operators and definition swaps can test transfer across surface changes.
works.borrow: Pair isomorphic dependency structures under different names and atoms.
works.adds: Executable semantics for grading each transferred rule.
works.note: Fluid perceptual interpretation is outside Opulse.

works.label: HR
works.title: Simon Colton, Alan Bundy, and Toby Walsh, Automatic Concept Formation in Pure Mathematics, 1999
works.idea: HR applies production rules to mathematical concepts, calculates examples, and develops conjectures from them. It evaluates ideas through the theory they help form.
works.opulse: Operator generation, examples, law analysis, and equivalence checks.
works.borrow: Score the fraction of invented operators that support useful new laws.
works.adds: Seeded concept families and a precise target for hidden operator recovery.

works.label: Gödel machine
works.title: Jürgen Schmidhuber, Gödel Machines, 2003
works.idea: A Gödel machine searches for a proof that rewriting part of its own software improves its specified utility, then performs a proved beneficial rewrite. Proof search and the utility definition are part of that software.
works.opulse: A test loop can accept a candidate operator when it improves a stated task objective.
works.borrow: Require a reproducible benefit certificate, including held out gain and compute cost.
works.adds: An interpreter for checking candidate operator behavior.
works.note: The interpreter checks values. It does not prove future utility or a beneficial self rewrite.

works.label: AIXI
works.title: Marcus Hutter, Universal Artificial Intelligence, 2005
works.idea: AIXI combines prediction about possible environments with actions chosen for expected future reward. It is a general sequential decision idealization.
works.opulse: Active queries to a hidden rule are actions chosen to improve later answers.
works.borrow: Define a query cost and terminal reward, then compare policies over complete interaction traces.
works.adds: A finite, executable rule environment.
works.note: Opulse does not implement AIXI or its universal prior.

works.label: Synthesis
works.title: Rajeev Alur and colleagues, Syntax Guided Synthesis, 2013
works.idea: Synthesis searches programs in a specified grammar against a logical specification. Counterexamples refine a candidate until it meets the specification or search fails.
works.opulse: The generated definition grammar and equivalence checker can support proposed rule revision.
works.borrow: Report candidate count, counterexample quality, and solver coverage.
works.adds: Fresh benchmark targets and traces of how a model arrived at a candidate.
works.note: Complete proofs depend on the supported solver fragment.

works.label: PowerPlay
works.title: Jürgen Schmidhuber, PowerPlay, 2013
works.idea: PowerPlay continually searches for a task the solver cannot solve at that stage and a solver change that handles it while retaining earlier skills. Task creation and skill retention are coupled.
works.opulse: A task loop can add operator tasks and recheck earlier tasks after each solver update.
works.borrow: Keep a cumulative task ledger and recheck earlier tasks after each update.
works.adds: Exact, automatically generated task solutions and dependency structure.
works.note: The link concerns a test protocol.

works.label: Program learning
works.title: Brenden Lake, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, and Joshua Tenenbaum, Human Level Concept Learning through Probabilistic Program Induction, 2015
works.idea: A handwritten character is represented by a generative program inferred from few examples. A learned concept is tested through recognition and generation.
works.opulse: A queried operator can be inferred as a program and applied to new inputs.
works.borrow: Test both rule identification and generation of informative new examples.
works.adds: Exact functional outputs and supported equivalence checks.
works.note: Visual uncertainty is absent from the usual integer setting.

works.label: bAbI
works.title: Jason Weston and colleagues, Towards AI Complete Question Answering, 2015
works.idea: bAbI uses small synthetic tasks to isolate prerequisites such as chaining facts and deduction. Separate task scores localize failure.
works.opulse: Substitution, branches, self calls and dependency depth have separate settings, and each task records the kinds and depth it actually uses.
works.borrow: Publish scores by required operation and number of relevant definitions.
works.adds: New generated rules and checked numerical consequences.

works.label: CLEVR
works.title: Justin Johnson and colleagues, CLEVR, 2017
works.idea: CLEVR builds questions from known functional programs and annotates their reasoning steps. Controlled question families expose shortcut strategies.
works.opulse: Expression trees and definition ablations have a similar diagnostic role.
works.borrow: Check accuracy by program shape and whether a definition can be ignored.
works.adds: New textual rules and exact checking of submitted rewrites.
works.note: Visual recognition is outside Opulse.

works.label: SCAN & COGS
works.title: Brenden Lake and Marco Baroni, Generalization without Systematicity, 2018; Najoung Kim and Tal Linzen, COGS, 2020
works.idea: These benchmarks test familiar parts in unfamiliar combinations or structural positions. Their splits ask whether knowing a primitive transfers to new use.
works.opulse: Known operators can appear only in new compositions or dependency positions at test time.
works.borrow: Separate operator novelty, composition novelty, and position novelty.
works.adds: The rules themselves can also be generated afresh, with exact step grading.

works.label: PCFG SET
works.title: Dieuwke Hupkes and colleagues, Compositionality Decomposed, 2020
works.idea: PCFG SET separates several forms of generalization, including systematicity, productivity, synonym substitution, and exceptions. A single compositionality score hides these differences.
works.opulse: Depth, equivalent operators, notation, and branching can each change independently.
works.borrow: Define separate score families and avoid averaging away a targeted failure.
works.adds: Executable generated definitions and exact trace records.

works.label: DreamCoder
works.title: Kevin Ellis and colleagues, DreamCoder, 2021
works.idea: A solver extracts recurring program fragments into a library and uses that library on later tasks. Library learning and task solving improve together over cycles.
works.opulse: Hidden operator reinvention and controlled operator frequency.
works.borrow: Compare held out success and description length before and after admitting a proposed operator.
works.adds: Known intermediate operators and exact behavioral equivalence checks where supported.

works.label: Length tests
works.title: Grégoire Delétang and colleagues, Neural Networks and the Chomsky Hierarchy, 2022 preprint, 2023 publication
works.idea: The study tests formal language tasks with different memory requirements and longer strings than those seen in training. Length extrapolation reveals limits hidden by short test sets.
works.opulse: Recursion unfoldings and expression depth impose longer computations.
works.borrow: Plot accuracy and first error depth against unfoldings, holding notation constant.
works.adds: New functions supplied as definitions and exact value traces.
works.note: Language recognition and function evaluation differ.

works.label: Grokking
works.title: Alethea Power and colleagues, Grokking, 2022
works.idea: Test generalization on small algorithmic data can improve long after training accuracy is high. This suggests tracking learning dynamics rather than only final scores.
works.opulse: Repeated expressions and unseen compositions can be monitored across checkpoints.
works.borrow: Plot both curves and distinguish learning an operator from learning its composition.
works.adds: Multiple new rule families and known dependencies.
works.note: The reported learning dynamic has not been established for Opulse.

works.label: Induction heads
works.title: Catherine Olsson and colleagues, In Context Learning and Induction Heads, 2022
works.idea: Induction heads implement a token continuation pattern and may contribute to using context in transformer models. Mechanistic claims require interventions, not only correct predictions.
works.opulse: Fresh symbols and renamed definitions test whether a model uses a supplied rule.
works.borrow: Intervene on candidate components and score the effect on newly defined operators versus familiar arithmetic.
works.adds: Exact semantics distinguish a right continuation from a right computation.
works.note: A mechanism study is separate from the task generator.

works.label: ROME & MEMIT
works.title: Kevin Meng and colleagues, Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT, 2022; Meng and colleagues, Mass Editing Memory in a Transformer, 2023
works.idea: ROME changes a targeted factual association in model weights. MEMIT studies many such edits together.
works.opulse: A changed low layer operator can be supplied in context or learned through a weight edit.
works.borrow: Measure update success, unrelated preservation, and downstream dependent accuracy separately.
works.adds: Exact before and after values for all generated dependent expressions.
works.note: Computed functions require different edits from single factual associations.

works.label: Stitch & LILO
works.title: Matthew Bowers and colleagues, Top Down Synthesis for Library Learning, 2023; Gabriel Grand and colleagues, LILO, 2024
works.idea: Stitch compresses a program corpus with reusable abstractions. LILO also studies names and documentation that make abstractions usable by language models.
works.opulse: Operator reuse and independent controls over names, notation, and frequency.
works.borrow: Measure compression and later use under opaque versus informative descriptions.
works.adds: Exact dependency closure and the ability to regenerate matched rule sets.

works.label: RippleEdits & MQuAKE
works.title: Roi Cohen and colleagues, RippleEdits, 2023; Zexuan Zhong and colleagues, MQuAKE, 2023
works.idea: An edited fact has consequences for related or multi step questions. Testing only the edited statement misses failed propagation.
works.opulse: Definition dependencies identify the downstream operators that may change.
works.borrow: Score effects by graph distance, and include unaffected controls.
works.adds: An exact dependency graph and recomputed values on a stated input sample after a definition edit.
works.note: The link concerns propagation tests. Real world factual dependencies are less explicit.

works.label: Physics of LMs
works.title: Tian Ye and colleagues, Physics of Language Models, Part 2.1, 2024
works.idea: Controlled synthetic math lets the authors study generalization and possible hidden reasoning processes. Their tasks separate learned procedure from repeated template use.
works.opulse: Fresh operator corpora and exact intermediate values support similar probes.
works.borrow: Probe whether model states encode selected intermediate outputs at each dependency layer.
works.adds: The operation rules can change between corpora.
works.note: The link concerns an experimental method.

works.label: Self play
works.title: Andrew Zhao and colleagues, Absolute Zero, 2025; Kefan Dong and Tengyu Ma, STP, 2025
works.idea: These systems use generated tasks and executable or formal feedback to train reasoning, with STP alternating conjecturing and proving. The feedback loop needs a source of valid tasks and a way to reject bad answers.
works.opulse: Concept self play can use the parser, interpreter, and solver for feedback.
works.borrow: Track task validity, novelty, accepted difficulty, and performance on untouched held out rules.
works.adds: Independently controllable rule factors and exact step checks.
works.note: The link concerns task generation. Gains from such a loop remain an empirical question.
